newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says 96 c/account gap seen at 3.2% of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says 96 c/account gap seen at 3.2% of GDP.

text.p: Jordan's current account balance of payments deficit is forecast to reach 3.2 percent of GDP in 1996, the finance minister said on Wednesday.
Marwan Awad told parliament in an speech on the 1997 budget that this was possible despite a forecast rise in the trade deficit in 1996.
The current account balance of payments deficit was expected to reach $235 million in 1996, slightly less than 1995 levels, he said. He gave no comparison figures for 1995.

Awad said exports -- including re-exports -- were expected to rise 8 percent to $1.913 billion while imports were expected to jump 16 percent to $4.287 billion. He attributed the trade imbalance to a large food import bill after record grain prices in the first half of 1996.
